objective.statement: Tell simple time from compound time by how the beat divides.
successCriteria: I know that in simple time every beat divides into two.
I know that in compound time every beat divides into three.
I know a compound beat is a dotted note.

explanation.text: Every time signature you have met so far is in simple time. In simple time the beat is a plain note, and it divides into two equal halves: a crotchet beat into two quavers, a minim beat into two crotchets.

music.textAlternative: A crotchet beat, then a crotchet beat divided into two beamed quavers.

explanation.caption: Simple time: the beat divides into two.

explanation.text: Compound time works differently. Every beat divides into three equal notes, not two. To hold three quavers, the beat has to be a dotted crotchet: a crotchet is two quavers, and the dot adds half as much again, one more quaver.

music.textAlternative: A dotted crotchet beat, then a dotted crotchet beat divided into three beamed quavers.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: dotted crotchet, 3 beamed together (quaver, quaver, quaver).

explanation.caption: Compound time: the beat is a dotted note and divides into three.

explanation.text: In Grade 2 you met the triplet, which squeezes three notes into one ordinary beat. Compound time is not the same thing: there, three is the normal way to divide every beat, so no sign is needed.
Simple time: beats divide into 2. Compound time: beats divide into 3, and the beat is a dotted note.

music.textAlternative: A dotted crotchet followed by three beamed quavers.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: dotted crotchet, 3 beamed together (quaver, quaver, quaver).

steps: Tap the dotted crotchet once: that is one beat.
Now tap three even quavers in the same length of time: that is one beat divided into three.
Three even notes in each beat is the sound of compound time.
demonstration.textAlternative: A dotted crotchet beat, then a beat divided into three quavers: both last the same time.

guided.prompt: Which of these beats belongs to compound time?

options.label: A crotchet divided into two quavers
A minim divided into two crotchets
A quaver divided into two semiquavers
A dotted crotchet divided into three quavers

feedback.correct: Yes: a dotted note that divides into three is compound.

mistakes.beat-count-wrong: Count the beats in one complete bar again — that gives the top number.
mistakes.beat-unit-wrong: The beat count is right, but what kind of note is each beat? That gives the bottom number.
mistakes.simple-compound-confusion: Do the beats split into two or into three? Two means simple time; three means compound.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Find the beat first, then count how many fit in a bar.

guided.prompt: In compound time the beat is a dotted crotchet. How many quavers last as long as one dotted crotchet?

2.reason: Two quavers last as long as a plain crotchet. The dot adds half as much again: one more quaver.

4.reason: Four quavers is a minim. A dotted crotchet is a crotchet (2 quavers) plus half of it (1 quaver).

6.reason: Six quavers is a dotted minim, two whole beats of compound time.

feedback.correct: Yes: a crotchet and one more quaver make three.

3.reason: Three equal parts is compound time, where the beat is a dotted note. An undotted beat divides into two.

4.reason: Four would be two sub-divisions of the beat. The first division of an undotted beat is into two equal parts.

6.reason: Six is far too many for one beat. The first division of an undotted beat is into two equal parts.

Compound time: each beat divides into three equal notes.
A compound beat is a dotted note, such as a dotted crotchet.
